caption: Performance of different triggers. The words used as triggers on the horizontal axis are arranged in ascending order according to the ASR of the clean model.
model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the Attack Success Rate (ASR) for different trigger words under three insertion strategies—“start,” “random,” and “end”—on the SST-2 dataset with a clean-label poisoning rate of 5% (2.6% of total). The horizontal axis displays trigger words arranged in ascending order of the clean model’s ASR: “bb,” “mb,” “cf,” “beautiful,” “excellent,” “gorgeous,” “wonderful,” “brilliant,” and “beautifully.” The vertical axis represents ASR, ranging from 0.2 to 0.9 with a linear scale and tick marks every 0.1 unit. The green line with circle markers (“start”) begins at an ASR of approximately 0.2 for “bb,” rises to about 0.75 for “mb,” dips to around 0.4 for “cf,” and then increases to nearly 0.9 for “beautifully.” The orange line with cross markers (“random”) starts at approximately 0.5 for “bb,” drops to about 0.2 for “cf,” and gradually rises to around 0.85 for “beautifully.” The purple line with circle markers (“end”) starts at about 0.5 for “bb,” peaks at approximately 0.9 for “mb,” then fluctuates, dipping to around 0.65 for “cf,” rising to about 0.8 for “excellent,” and ending at approximately 0.85 for “beautifully.”
